findings.text: non-blocking: _requested_field_names at reckon/mcp.py:338 is a verbatim copy of the function the repository already owns at reckon/crew/query.py:104 — the same four branches and the same comprehension, body for body, with one word of the docstring changed — so the parsing of one crew request's field list now has two owners that can drift exactly as the vocabulary did. The owner module is already imported by this diff for RUN_SCOPES, RUN_SOURCES, LIVE_OVERRUN_FIELDS and LIVE_PLACEMENT_FIELDS, so importing _requested_field_names from it is the whole repair. The promotion-time clone detector in reckon/clones.py scans for textual copies and may flag this.

non-blocking: _LIVE_ROW_FIELDS (reckon/mcp.py:263-327) re-declares, as a static literal, the live field vocabulary that reckon/crew/query.py:152 _live_field_vocabulary already owns and derives from classify_pointer({}) plus LIVE_OVERRUN_FIELDS, LIVE_PLACEMENT_FIELDS and COMMON_RUN_FIELDS (reckon/crew/query.py:175-181). The addition does not extend the owner, because the owner cannot run without opening storage (classify_pointer reads worker.json/exit.json/attempt.json), which is why the storage-free copy exists; test_the_refusal_vocabulary_covers_every_live_field now detects drift between the two, but the fork remains, and the node's own manifest records this as follow-on (1). Naming the reason here so the exemption is explicit rather than silent.

non-blocking: the view pre-flight compares the raw argument against VIEW_NAMES, where the view's own validator strips and lowercases first (reckon/mcp_views.py:2090, selected = (view or 'summary').strip().lower()). A request mcp._read_plan_tool(project='fixture', view='RAW') answered before this change — the base revision passed 'RAW' straight to _read_plan, which normalizes at reckon/mcp.py:1540 — is now refused with invalid_view, so a well-formed request is refused where a malformed one was meant to be. The same raw comparison sits at reckon/mcp.py:2182 for ROADMAP_TOOL_VIEWS. Narrow (a case or whitespace variant of a documented name, and view is typed str | None so no schema constrains it), hence non-blocking, but it is a behaviour regression on the tool surface.

non-blocking: the field pre-flight is guarded by 'view == "live"', so a crew request with view='runs' and an unknown field still reads the pointers and the ledger before query._refuse_unknown_fields refuses it at reckon/crew/query.py:115 (reached through _selected_fields at reckon/crew/query.py:147). The plan's §17 Change requires that 'Field names ... are checked against their declared vocabularies first' for the four tools; the runs view carries its own vocabulary and is not covered, so the requirement is met for one of the two views that take fields. The done_when named only the live case, which is why this is a gap against the plan rather than against the gate.

non-blocking: assert "dispatched_at" in detail compares the refusal text against the name the test itself passed in, so the two sides move together and the assertion stays green for a checker that refused every field name. It is not the guard — _refuse()'s assert not stub.reached is independent and does the work — but no case in the file asserts the opposite direction, that a valid live field list is still served, which is why the class of false refusal at reckon/mcp.py:1222 passes this gate. Noted here rather than in the durability justification because durability does not rest on this line.

non-blocking: the module docstring carries incident and changelog prose rather than mechanism — 'on 2026-10-23 a crew view live call naming an unknown field waited over 120 s before it was refused' (lines 7-8) — which the repository's comment rule forbids in source, since the tracker owns the bug-to-code link. The mechanism sentence beside it ('Refusing it after the first file read makes the answer wait on whatever storage is doing') carries the same information without the dated incident.

FINDING reckon/mcp.py:338 non-blocking: _requested_field_names is a verbatim copy of the function the repository already owns at reckon/crew/query.py:104, so the parsing of one request's field list has two owners that can drift; the owner module is already imported by this diff.
FINDING reckon/mcp.py:263 non-blocking: _LIVE_ROW_FIELDS is a static re-declaration of the vocabulary reckon/crew/query.py:152 owns, not an extension of it, held to the owner only by a test; the storage-free requirement is why the copy exists, and the node records the resulting drift risk as follow-on (1).
FINDING reckon/mcp.py:1222 non-blocking: the view pre-flight compares the raw argument against VIEW_NAMES while the view's owner strips and lowercases at reckon/mcp_views.py:2090, so view='RAW' is refused where it was served before; the same shape is at reckon/mcp.py:2182.
FINDING reckon/mcp.py:372 non-blocking: the field pre-flight covers only view='live', so a malformed crew view='runs' fields request still reads the pointers and the ledger before reckon/crew/query.py:115 refuses it, leaving the plan's §17 field-name requirement delivered for one of the two field-taking views.
FINDING tests/test_a_malformed_request_is_refused_before_storage.py:61 non-blocking: the assertion compares the refusal text against the name the test passed in, so it moves with its own input and would pass for a checker that refused every field name; no case asserts a valid live field list is still served.
FINDING tests/test_a_malformed_request_is_refused_before_storage.py:7 non-blocking: the module docstring states a dated incident where the repository's comment rule asks for mechanism.
